# Independent upstream CHM corpus (test-only)

These archives are **unmodified upstream bytes**, not CHMs generated by chm-kit.
`expected/` contains all 721 non-directory resources extracted by the installed
7-Zip 26.05 (`7zz t` then `7zz x`), including internal metadata/index resources.
`manifest.json` pins every archive, resource and license SHA-256, source commit
URL, raw Git blob where applicable, layout observations and the independent
oracle command/version. `SHA256SUMS` also pins the manifest itself. Never replace
an oracle with chm-kit's output to make a test pass.

Release CHMs are not claimed to be Git blobs or reproducible builds. The source
commits identify the corresponding releases; official download URLs and archive
hashes identify the actual binary test inputs.

The 7-Zip CHM was extracted with the already-installed trusted `7zz` from the
1,589,510-byte official installer (SHA-256
`26cb6e9f56333682122fafe79dbcdfd51e9f47cc7217dccd29ac6fc33b5598cd`).
**The installer was never executed and is not retained.** Its member `7-zip.chm`
was renamed without changing bytes; `License.txt` is retained as `LICENSE.7zip`.
No unknown executable was run. PuTTY's notice was copied unchanged from
`putty-0.83/LICENCE` in the official source tarball; its URL/hash are in the
manifest. Existing `../pychm-example/` was neither edited nor regenerated.

## Malformed archives

Eleven small samples from [libmspack commit
55d501976171397ccd5d5a7a1ca7da065b1d9a06](https://github.com/kyz/libmspack/tree/55d501976171397ccd5d5a7a1ca7da065b1d9a06/libmspack/test/test_files/chmd)
cover zero reset interval, name bounds/overread, negative span info, off-by-one,
blank/Unicode filenames and oversized 32-/64-bit ENCINTs. libmspack distributes
these under its LGPL license (`LICENSE.libmspack`); they have no separate
per-fixture license notice. Exact per-file source URLs and hashes are pinned.

`cve-2015-4467-reset-interval-zero.chm.xor` remains upstream XOR-obfuscated bytes;
the test XORs 0xFF **only in memory**, matching upstream `chmd_test.c`. Do not
open these samples in a desktop CHM viewer or execute their contents. Several
are upstream-generated ITSF v2 **malformed** structures with invalid directory
lengths. They do **not** establish working normal ITSF v2 interoperability, and
strict early rejection does not establish that later corrupt fields were reached.

## Integrity, licensing and scope

- **All content here is test-only and must stay out of npm**, especially GPL
  PyCHM data and its extracted derivatives. No blanket MIT relicensing applies.
- Raw/extracted bytes retain upstream licenses and notices, including notices
  inside the documents. Preserve `test/fixtures/** -text` and the fixture
  Prettier exclusion; do not normalize CRLF, NULs, HTML or binary resources.
- To reproduce oracle extraction **offline** with a trusted installed 7zz/7z:
  `python3 test/conformance/refresh-oracles.py` from the repository root. This
  checks pinned input/notice hashes first, uses no chm-kit module and performs no
  network downloads. It rewrites only this new fixture's expected bytes/manifest.
  Different 7-Zip versions change the tool-version/manifest hash, so review diffs.
- Valid real ITSF v2 remains missing. Other uncovered combinations include real
  GBK/UTF-16 text, LZXC v1, windows outside 64/128 KiB, and real long reset groups.
  A synthetic GBK writer differential is not a real GBK upstream corpus.
- CHMLib's main source tree contained no CHM; libmspack's tree contained malformed
  CHM tests but no normal CHM. The CHMLib Rust binding's 1.6 MB
  `topics.classic.chm` was investigated then excluded because its complete
  HelpStudio/third-party content redistribution rights could not be established.
  No large unknown-copyright assets are retained.
